module: D10-08 缺貨／供需缺口事件
objective: Define a replayable Taiwan shortage/supply-gap event state that cannot be inferred from supplier-delivery time alone.

SUPPLY_GAP_CONFIRMED_SOURCE_STATE: Explicit shortage/allocation/capacity-constraint evidence from a dated source is required.
At least one operational consequence must also be present: lead-time stress, production scheduling impact, inventory response or input-price pressure.
Demand is stored as a separate dimension and is not required to be strong.
SUPPLY_GAP_CANDIDATE: Indirect stress such as long supplier delivery or high input prices exists but explicit shortage/allocation evidence is absent.
MISMATCH_OR_BUFFERING_STATE: Lead time or inventory stress exists while fresh-order momentum weakens or customer inventory rises; do not call this a clean shortage-demand boom.
NO_CONFIRMED_GAP: Explicit shortage/allocation evidence is absent and operational stress evidence does not jointly support a supply-gap state.
UNKNOWN: Required evidence is missing, scope-incompatible or publication timing is not authenticated.

evidence: Overall manufacturing new orders 63.3 and production 62.7.
Key-material suppliers were described as capacity-limited and using selective order acceptance / quota allocation.
Electronics/optical new orders and production were both 47.7 despite a high composite PMI 65.5.
Official release explicitly cited material shortages, allocation, long lead times and rising key-material prices.
Supply bottlenecks and cost increases were stated to constrain some order and production scheduling.
53.1% of manufacturing respondents identified raw-material/key-component shortages as a concern.
Under Middle East conflict effects, reported delivery time increased 31.7% on average and 16.7% reported delivery-time uncertainty.
86.9% reported supply-chain risk-management actions; 78.9% advanced orders/lengthened preparation and 73.2% increased safety stock.
Electronics/optical supplier delivery 73.8 and input prices 83.3.
New-order momentum slowed, unfinished-order expansion decelerated to 54.3 and inventory rose to 64.8; customer inventory reached 51.0.

falsification: Long supplier delivery can be caused by geopolitics, logistics or material mismatch rather than demand acceleration.
High input prices can coexist with weak or slowing orders.
Inventory accumulation can be a defensive buffer or forced accumulation, not proof of shortage severity.
An industry shortage state does not prove any individual issuer has more backlog, higher ASP, better margin or higher stock return.
A shortage in one component can coexist with excess inventory elsewhere; long/short material mismatch must remain explicit.
pitRules: Never backdate a release to the observation month.
Do not fill missing event dimensions from later releases.
Keep survey category, formal industry and issuer product exposure as separate taxonomies.
Any issuer-level use requires independent issuer-native product/revenue/order evidence.
No fixed bullish/bearish sign is assigned to a supply-gap state.
promotionReason: A dedicated, replayable Taiwan event contract can now be populated from dated official NDC/CIER releases with explicit shortage/allocation language, operational consequences, demand state, inventory state and negative-control months. This proves PIT/source feasibility only; it does not establish predictive efficacy or issuer-level effects.
exactNext: Accumulate independent future shortage/supply-gap events under the same contract and preserve source-family identity.
Add issuer-native shortage/allocation or capacity evidence before mapping any event to a listed company.
Only after multiple independent dates and issuer mappings exist may D10-08 enter L4 prospective/OOS effect testing.
